newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo's top garment maker seeks listing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Colombo's top garment maker seeks listing in 1997.

text.p: Tri-Star Apparel Exports (Pte) Ltd, Sri Lanka's largest garment manufacturer, will seek listing on the Colombo stock exchange next year to help slash its cost of borrowings, a top company official said on Thursday.
Tri-Star which is an associate of SR Gent Plc, provides the bulk of its output to British stores chain Marks & Spencer, Managing Director Kumar Dewapura said.
Tri-Star was Sri Lanka's top foreign exchange earning company in 1995 when its earning totalled 3.2 billion rupees ($58.18 million), according to Sri Lanka Customs Department statistics.
"The company will seek a listing on the Colombo Stock Exchange mainly to reduce interest cost since equity is far cheaper than debt," Dewapura told Reuters.
Tri-Star, which now has 27 garment factories and employs 24,600 people, needs cheaper source of funds for expansion, he said.
"What is holding us back is high interest rates in the country. Tri-Star paid 160 million rupees in interest on rupee loans in 1995," he said.
